o.text: Borrowed from Arabic يَا (yā, “o, hey, you”).
Borrowed from Classical Persian یا (yā, “either, or”).

According to most scholars, a derivation of Persian یار (yâr).
Alternatively, from a barely attested stem *yar-, in which case possibly related to *yara- (“to be good enough”). See Turkish yardım for Turkic cognates.
From Middle Mongol ᠬᠦᠷᠭᠡᠨ (kürgen) (compare modern Mongolian хүргэн (xürgen)). Cognate with Khalaj kurəkən (“son-in-law”), dialectal Turkish köregen (“son-in-law”).
